rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Player Area 3 Game Play 3.1 Phase 1 3.2 Phase 2 4 Game End 4.1 Scoring Overview Microcosm is a deck building game where the aim is to have more influence than your opponent at the end of the game. Influence can be earned by: • Owning colonies • Owning spoils • Owning capitals • Researching technologies • Collecting red, yellow, green or purple Domain cards, Colonies or Spoils You score influence at the end of the game, determined by the scoring conditions you have managed to add to your deck and from the Colonies and Spoils that you own. Player Area As the game progresses, your player area in front of you, will comprise of: • Played Card: The current Domain card you have played and are resolving. Face up. • Colonies: Planets acquired by playing a Colonize action. Face down unless revealed. You can check all available colonies for reference on this image: https://boardgamegeek.com/image/2521243/eminent-domain-microcosm • Discards: Cards you have already played and resolved. Face up. • Spoils: Planets or Colonies won by successfully performing a Warfare action. • Technologies: Technologies that you have acquired. Face up Game Play You start the game without any cards in your hand and will gradually build your own deck of cards as the game progresses. Each turn consists of 2 phases. Beginning with the starting player, take a turn to perform the following 2 phases: Phase 1 Either take one of the 3 face up cards in the supply, replacing the taken card with the top card from the draw deck. OR If you don’t like what is available from the supply, then you may take the top card from the draw deck instead. Phase 2 Play an action by placing a card from your hand in front of you and resolving the text on the card. Then place the card in your discard pile. OR Pick up some or all of the cards in your discard pile and put them into your hand. (In Phase 2, when picking up discards you may pick up as many as you wish. You don't have to pick up the whole discard pile. There are some cards that are useful to leave in your discard pile.) Game End When the draw deck is exhausted, continue play without refilling the supply. After the last card is drawn from the supply, the active player finishes their turn and the game ends. Scoring Players collect all cards from their hands and discard piles (keep your colonies and spoils separate) and determine their Influence: • The Influence calculated from each scoring condition shown on your Domain cards • The Influence shown on any Colonies and Spoils owned The sum of these is your final Influence score. The player with the most influence wins. In the case of a tie, the player who played second wins.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] WOW: really had a hard time understanding what we were supposed to do in this game. The instructions are "thin" and not very illuminating. the terminology was inconsistent. maybe there is a how-to-play video somewhere that can help. At least it is a short game

[Rating: 1/10] #1 Issue: CANNOT play the game with the rules that come in the box!  It assumes knowledge of Eminent Domain and leaves out critical information on how a turn works, what cards do what, what everything on a card means, has no/minimal images to help, etc.  Additionally, extra cards come as promos without any mention of what they are for, including Eminent Domain (board game) which confuses the issue with the above mentioned issues. In other words some cards in the Eminent Domain: Microcosm game say Eminent Domain on them, but are not used in the game, without ever knowing that they should be rem

[Rating: 2/10] This is a short 2 player card game that uses the theme from Eminent Domain. We sort of muddled our way through it, but the game didn't come with a proper rulebook, so we had a lot of rules questions and confusion through the entire game. There might be a good game here, for awhile I was too frustrated with it to give it another fair try. I revisited it after some time, and found it to be pretty unremarkable.

[Rating: 2/10] Until an official rulebook that is complete and explains its concepts fully is released, this game is unplayable as packaged.  If you scour the rules forum and watch videos apparently you can play it, but that onus should not be on the buyer to figure that out.

[Rating: 2/10] Only played on BGA. The rules are only 2 pages but basically provide no guidance about what you're supposed to be doing and expect you to figure it out by reading the cards.  I had played Eminent Domain a long time ago and I think these rules assume that you are already familiar with those rules.  We are not the target audience for these types of fast 2-player only card games, so I wouldn't have likely wanted to play again either way, but the poor rules made even learning game once time wasted I can never get back.

[Rating: 2/10] I tend to quite enjoy micro games, but does 36 cards even count as a micro? This could've just as well been a full deck of 54 or 60 cards. The odd thing is that gameplay seemed both terribly restrictive and on rails, and also somewhat intriguing. I need to play it again to firm up my opinion, but cannot see myself searching it out.

[Rating: 3/10] The rule book is confusing.  I thought if I just started playing I would get it but no.  I surrender.

[Rating: 3/10] I know a little card game. Not much to it but there is some strategy and some luck which makes it fun for a micro game.
